newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Tata Electric plans $300 mln debt issue.
newsitem.headline: India's Tata Electric plans $300 mln debt issue.

text.p: Indian power utility Tata Electric Companies plans a global debt issue of $300 million, merchant bankers said on Tuesday.
About half the issue will be repayable in 10 years and the balance in 20 years, they said.

The firm has sought ministry of finance approval for the issue under new guidelines which exempts loans of a maturity of 10 years or more from an annual ceiling on external commercial borrowings, bankers said.
Company officials were not immediately available for comment.
Tata Electric Companies (TEC) make up India's largest private sector power utility, generating and supplying power in bulk to the Bombay region.
TEC consists of three separate entities - Tata Hydro-Electric Power, Andhra Valley Power and Tata Power -- all belonging to India's leading business house of Tatas.
The issue will finance TEC's capital expenditure programme, including a grassroot 450 MW combined cycle plant at Bhivpuri in western India, bankers said.
"They have received all (pending) permissions from the state government," one banker said.
TEC is in the process of finalising specifications for an international competitive bidding for the project, they said.
The company expects to spend over 10 percent of the cost of the Bhivpuri project -- estimated at 13.0 billion rupees -- in the current financial year, bankers said.
